## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `SetupGuide`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `github-setup-guide`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **SetupGuide**.

## Step 2: Access GitHub settings

1. <!-- manual: Log in to your GitHub account. -->
2. <!-- manual: Click on your profile picture in the top-right corner of the page. -->
3. Select **Settings** from the dropdown menu.

## Step 3: Navigate to developer settings

1. <!-- manual: Scroll down in the left sidebar of the Settings page. -->
2. Select **Developer settings** near the bottom.

## Step 4: Go to personal access tokens

1. In the Developer settings page, select **Personal access tokens**.
2. Select **Tokens (classic)** or **Fine-grained tokens** depending on your preference.

## Step 5: Generate a new token

1. Select **Generate new token**.
2. <!-- manual: Provide a descriptive Note for the token (e.g., Ballerina GitHub Connector). -->
3. <!-- manual: Set an Expiration period appropriate for your use case. -->
4. <!-- manual: Select the required Scopes based on the operations you intend to use: -->
5. <!-- manual: repo: Full control of private repositories (required for most repository operations). -->
6. <!-- manual: read:org: Read organization and team membership. -->
7. <!-- manual: read:user: Read user profile data. -->
8. <!-- manual: admin:org: Full control of orgs and teams (if managing organization resources). -->
9. <!-- manual: delete_repo: Delete repositories (if needed). -->
10. <!-- manual: gist: Create and manage gists. -->
11. <!-- manual: notifications: Access notifications. -->
12. Select **Generate token** at the bottom of the page.
13. <!-- manual: Copy the generated token immediately: it will not be shown again. -->

## Step 6: Open webhook settings

1. <!-- manual: Go to your GitHub repository. -->
2. Select **Settings** → **Webhooks** → **Add webhook**.
